High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Jabalpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Shri Ajay Tamrakar - Govt. Advocate for the respondent/

Heard on I.A.No.18696/2025, which is first application under Section 430(1) of B.N.S.S.,
2023/389(1) of Cr.P.C. for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to appellant Pradeep @ Babloo Prajapati.

The appellant is aggrieved of the judgment dated 05.03.2021 passed by the Learned Special Judge (POCSO Act)/23 rd Additional Sessions Judge, Bhopal (M.P.) in ST No.377/2019, whereby appellant has been convicted and sentenced as under:-
 Conviction Sentence  
 Section Act Imprisonment Fine  
 376 I.P.C. R.I. for 20 years Rs.2,000/- 
 366 A I.P.C. R.I. for 7 years Rs.1,000/- 
 363 I.P.C. R.I. for 3 years Rs.500/- 
Learned counsel for the appellant submits that as per version of the prosecutrix she had left her home on her own volition as is narrated by P.W.- 3 Dr. Vaishali Chaurasiya.

It is submitted that FSL report Ex.P-16 is not clear and no human sperms or semen was found on various objects recovered from the victim whereas, slide of the appellant E-1, E-2 did not contain 2 CRA-5046-2021 sufficient semen spots to conduct serum examination.

It is submitted that lady Doctor advised ossification test as is mentioned by her in her report Ex.P-3 and also deposed in para 3 of her examination-in-chief,
but no X-ray report is brought on record, therefore, in the light of the judgment passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sunil Vs. State of Haryana, (2010) 1 SCC 742 , it is submitted that when first school Dakhila Kharij Register is not available as is deposed by P.W.-4 that victim had taken admission in Class-III and she had also not brought on record the T.C., on the basis of which, date of Pradeep Alias Babloo Prajapati vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128760472/
1 birth of the victim was recorded.

sentences.text: It is submitted that there are good chances of success of the appeal.
He, therefore, prays for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to the appellant.
Learned Government Advocate, in his turn, opposes the application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to the appellant.

After hearing learned counsel for the parties and going through the record, without commenting on the merits of the case, we are of the considered opinion that this is a fit case to suspend the remaining jail sentence of the present appellant and to release him on bail.

Accordingly, I.A. No.
18696 of 2025 is allowed.

It is directed that on depositing the fine amount, if not already deposited and on furnishing a personal bond to the tune of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with two solvent sureties in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Trial Court for his appearance before the Trial Court on 27.02.2026 and on such other dates as may be fixed by the Trial Court, the execution of remaining part of jail sentence imposed upon appellant Pradeep 3 CRA-5046-2021 @ Babloo Prajapati shall remain suspended and he shall be released on bail till final disposal of the appeal.
List the matter for final hearing in due course.
 (VIVEK AGARWAL) (RATNESH CHANDRA SIN  JUDGE JUDGE  sp/-
